overview: The National Cemetery Administration is the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs that runs national cemeteries for veterans and provides headstones, markers, and other burial honors. This bill would require the VA to send Congress a yearly report on the agency's work and post it online. The report would include burial counts by cemetery, by category of eligible person, and by casket or cremation, a measure of family and customer satisfaction, maps of national cemeteries and of state, county, and tribal veterans cemeteries that receive VA grants, and burial options at each open national cemetery. It would also count headstones, markers, medallions, and presidential memorial certificates provided, burials of unclaimed veterans' remains, and list completed and planned construction projects and grants with their recipients, amounts, and purposes. As of October 6, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar for a vote.
for: Supporters say a single public yearly report gives veterans, families, and Congress a clear picture of burial services, construction plans, and grants, making it easier to spot gaps in service.
against: Critics say much of this information is already tracked or available elsewhere, so a new detailed report mainly adds paperwork for the agency rather than improving burial services.
